summary: Iteration 10: verified boot-resilience hardening (ms_graph lazy Fernet + startup try/except) did NOT break auth. 8/8 backend tests pass: /api/auth/me returns 401 (backend up); server.py imports successfully in a fresh subprocess with TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY unset; server.py startup() wraps create_index calls and _seed_admin in try/except; ms_graph.py uses _get_fernet() lazy accessor (no module-level Fernet); fresh registration + first-login MFA setup + /me works; existing admin login+MFA works; credentialed CORS still reflects Origin https://campaigns.koodh.com with Allow-Credentials: true.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py startup() correctly wraps three independent try/except blocks (storage init, index init, seed admin) so a failure in one section does not abort lifespan startup — exactly what fixes the prod 502 crash-loop.

ms_graph.py imports cryptography.fernet at module scope but only instantiates Fernet inside _get_fernet(); missing TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY now raises only when token cache load/save is exercised, not at import time. Verified via isolated subprocess import.
server.py is ~1400 LOC — consider splitting auth, campaigns, contacts, admin into modules in a future iteration for maintainability (non-blocking).
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral bootfix_<uuid>@example.com user created per run for registration+MFA flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Hardening verified on preview. Prod 502 could not be reproduced (preview env has TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY set). If prod still 502s after redeploy, inspect prod backend logs for the specific exception raised during startup that the new try/except now swallows and logs. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_iter10_boot_resilience.py as regression.
rca of the issue: Prod 502 was caused by an unhandled exception during FastAPI lifespan startup (likely either Fernet(os.environ['TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY']) at ms_graph import when the env var was missing/invalid in prod, or a create_index/seed_admin failure). Mitigation: (a) Fernet is now lazily instantiated inside _get_fernet() so import cannot crash; (b) startup() wraps index creation and _seed_admin in try/except with logger.error so the app boots and serves /api even if those side effects fail. Verified by (1) subprocess importing server.py after popping TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, (2) full auth regression (register, MFA setup+verify, admin login, /me, CORS).
